newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower in consolidation.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower in consolidation.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended lower in what traders said was a light-volume consolidation.
Reduced fears of winterkill in wheat also undermined KCBT wheat values, traders said.
"Wheat in Kansas City and Chicago is responding to overbought conditions today. We're getting a light-volume setback," a KCBT trader said at the close.
KCBT wheat settled 1-1/2 to 2-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with March down 2-1/4 cents at $4.15-3/4. July was down 2-1/2 cents at $3.64-1/2.
Losses in wheat were tempered by late spillover support from CBOT soybeans, traders said.
Term Commodities bought 1.2 million July bushels. Benson-Quinn sold 800,000 March and bought 500,000 each of March and July.
